title: loadpath antenna brief
description: `loadpath antenna`: a board antenna solved in what surrounds it (antenna.py, rf.py). Maxwell's equations in the time domain on the board's copper, its laminate, the printed shell with its measured permittivity and loss, and the metal near it: the reflection (S11) across the band, the resonance and how far the surroundings move it, the input impedance, radiation and total efficiency with the heat split by material, and a sensitivity field (what a piece of plastic or metal at each point would do to the port). Inside a product, give the same block as a component's `antenna` in an enclosure brief.

band.description: MHz: the band the radio uses, e.g. [2400, 2483.5]

sweep.description: MHz: the range solved (default: the band widened by 30% of its centre each way)

size.description: mm: a rectangular board, its corner at the origin, its bottom face at z = 0

outline.description: a closed outline, [x, y] mm in the board's frame (its corner at the origin)

thickness.description: mm (default 1.6); the top copper is at z = thickness

anyOf.description: a material with radio-frequency values on file: fr4, pla, petg, abs, tpu, pa12, pa11, air; or 'metal'

base.description: the material whose values are used where none is given

fill.description: share of the volume that is solid, the rest air (a lattice's relative density; for a printed part its mass over its solid mass, which is more than the slicer's infill setting because walls and skins are solid). The effective permittivity is taken between the Hashin-Shtrikman bounds

source.description: where the values come from (kept in the report)
